docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
TALISMAN is a Python package for summarizing gene set functions using large language models (LLMs).

It uses the OntoGPT package to interface with LLMs.

For more details, please see the full documentation.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
TALISMAN uses uv to manage its environment:

git clone https://github.com/monarch-initiative/talisman.git
cd talisman
uv sync
uv run talisman --help

uv sync creates .venv with the versions locked in uv.lock, including the dev tools, and installs talisman in editable mode. .python-version selects Python 3.11: on Apple Silicon the locked lxml 5.0.0 has no wheels for Python 3.9 or 3.10. The lock supports Python 3.9 to 3.11 (its semsimian has no wheels for newer versions). Run the unit tests with uv run python -m unittest discover tests.unit.

docs.title: Functionality
docs.text:
The goal of gene summary enrichment is to assemble a textual summary of the functions of a set of genes and their products.

TALISMAN can run in three different ways:

  1. Map gene symbols to IDs using the resolver (unless IDs are specified)
  2. Fetch gene descriptions using Alliance API
  3. Create a prompt using descriptions

Options:

  • -r, --resolver TEXT - OAK selector for the gene ID resolver, e.g., sqlite:obo:hgnc for HGNC gene IDs.
  • -C, --context TEXT - domain, e.g., anatomy, industry, health-related
  • --strict / --no-strict - If set, there must be a unique mappings from labels to IDs. Defaults to True.
  • -U, --input-file TEXT - Path to a file with gene IDs to enrich if not passed as arguments.
  • --randomize-gene-descriptions-using-file TEXT - For evaluation only. Path to a file containing gene identifiers and descriptions; if this option is used, TALISMAN will swap out gene descriptions with those from this gene set file.
  • --ontological-synopsis / --no-ontological-synopsis - If set, use automated rather than manual gene descriptions. Defaults to True.
  • --combined-synopsis / --no-combined-synopsis - If set, combine gene descriptions. Defaults to False.
  • --end-marker TEXT - Specify a character or string to end prompts with. For testing minor variants of prompts.
  • --annotations / --no-annotations - If set, include annotations in the prompt. Defaults to True.
  • --prompt-template TEXT - Path to a file containing the prompt.
  • --interactive / --no-interactive - Interactive mode - rather than call the API, the function will present a walkthrough process. Defaults to False.

Example (requires an OpenAI API key via export OPENAI_API_KEY=... or uv run runoak set-apikey -e openai <key>):

uv run talisman enrichment -r sqlite:obo:hgnc -U tests/input/genesets/EDS.yaml -o eds.yaml

In this case, the prompt will include gene summaries retrieved from the Alliance of Genome Resources database. To summarize a list of pre-selected ontology term names directly without gene description lookup, set lacks_descriptions: true in the input YAML (see tests/input/genesets/microbiome.yaml).

The response text will include, among other fields, a summary like this:

Summary: The common function among these genes is their involvement in the regulation and organization of the extracellular matrix, particularly collagen fibril organization and biosynthesis.

docs.title: Summarize AmiGO 3 enrichment results with Claude
docs.text:
talisman amigo3-summarize grounds the summary in statistics. It runs a gene set through the enrichment methods of AmiGO 3:

method tests the genes against significant when go GO terms, hypergeometric over-representation FDR (BH) <= 0.05 mgsa GO terms, Bayesian model-based gene set analysis posterior >= 0.5 gocam genes of each GO-CAM model FDR (BH) <= 0.05 neighborhood connected neighborhoods of the GO-CAM gene network FDR (BY) <= 0.05 network GO-term connectivity in the GO-CAM gene network FDR (BY) <= 0.05

Claude then reads each method's significant sets and writes a summary, a mechanism and themes that cite their IDs. Every cited ID is checked against those tables (ungrounded_ids) and every cited gene against the input (unknown_genes). With --agent, Claude can also query the AmiGO 3 database read-only while it writes, through the same tools as AmiGO 3's chat.

Requirements:

  • A running AmiGO 3 server (default http://127.0.0.1:8030, or pass --amigo3-url). To build and run one locally (requires uv and a Rust toolchain for genesets/MGSA): bash git clone https://github.com/geneontology/amigo3-prototype.git git clone https://github.com/geneontology/ai-gene-review.git cd amigo3-prototype uv sync uv run amigo3 fetch uv run amigo3 build --repository ../ai-gene-review uv run amigo3 serve --backend duckdb --genesets-url '' (No Solr or Docker needed. Without --repository, only go and mgsa work; the others are reported in skipped_methods.)
  • Claude Code, signed in (claude auth status). TALISMAN runs claude -p, so calls are billed to that sign-in; set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to choose between accounts. No API key is needed.
uv run talisman amigo3-summarize -U tests/input/genesets/HALLMARK_GLYCOLYSIS.yaml --max-budget-usd 0.50 -o /tmp/glycolysis.yaml
uv run talisman amigo3-summarize --agent --amigo3-dir ../amigo3-prototype --max-budget-usd 0.50 -m sonnet HK1 PFKM PKM ENO1

Useful options: --methods (default go,mgsa,gocam,neighborhood), --aspect P|F|C|all (or comma-separated, e.g. P,C), --max-terms (default 50, balancing top p-values, MGSA support and study-gene coverage), --evidence all|no_iea|experimental|iba, --species (an AmiGO 3 species key; default the gene set's taxon), --gene-descriptions (also give Claude the gene descriptions from the enrichment command), --max-budget-usd and --show-prompt.

Output is YAML. Besides the summary, mechanism, themes and caveats it records the genes AmiGO 3 could not use (unresolved_genes, ambiguous_genes, untested_genes), the rows each method showed the model (enrichment), every significant set (significant_ids), and three grounding checks: ungrounded_ids (cited, but in no table), nonsignificant_ids (cited, but only from a row listed as context) and misattributed_ids (cited in a theme whose listed methods do not match the tables containing the ID).

Replies are cached in .talisman_claude_cache.db in the current directory (or the talisman --cache-db path), keyed by model name (incorporating ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL overrides and also indexed under the resolved model ID reported by Claude), prompt and tools; pass --no-cache for a fresh answer. Agent-mode runs that complete without tool queries (num_turns <= 2) are not cached. An alias such as sonnet keeps its cached replies after it moves to a newer model, so pass a full model name when that matters.

talisman amigo3-benchmark runs AmiGO 3's bundled example gene sets (11 human sets), each with curated expected GO terms, and reports the recall of those terms (filtered to the tested --aspect, or across all aspects with --aspect all) by:

  • claude: the GO IDs Claude cites from significant table rows
  • go_top: the same number of top hypergeometric GO terms, for a like-for-like comparison
  • shown: every significant GO term shown to Claude
  • go_all and mgsa_all: every significant hypergeometric term (often hundreds) and every MGSA-active term

It runs one set by default; pass --limit 0 for all of them, or --set-id to pick sets. On AmiGO 3 build 77fbebffd9d35f96 across all 11 human example gene sets, the enrichment and table-selection baselines recover:

aspect source mean terms exact recall specific recall (+ descendants) P (60 BP expected terms) shown (--max-terms 50) 45.5 28.5% 40.0% P (60 BP expected terms) go_all 534.1 62.4% 67.3% P (60 BP expected terms) mgsa_all 12.1 4.8% 18.5% all (71 P,F,C expected terms) shown (--max-terms 50) 67.0 25.5% 35.1% all (71 P,F,C expected terms) go_all 682.9 63.9% 69.3% all (71 P,F,C expected terms) mgsa_all 67.1 5.6% 23.6%

docs.title: Tabular GO Enrichment and Summarization (tabular-enrichment and tabular-summarize)
docs.text:
For organisms not in AmiGO 3 or custom correlation/expression workbooks (.xlsx, .tsv, or .csv with a genes incldg GO table containing gene_id, go_id, go_ontology, go_term, Significant?, pos/neg corr, r (Pearson), FPKM average (samples), and hypothetical protein?), TALISMAN provides built-in statistical enrichment and grounded Claude summarization:

# 1. Run one-sided hypergeometric over-representation and two-sided Mann-Whitney U rank tests
uv run talisman tabular-enrichment workbook.xlsx results/

# 2. Summarize significant (FDR <= 0.05) and suggestive (FDR <= 0.25) terms with Claude Code
uv run talisman tabular-summarize results/ both --context-file experiment_context.txt

tabular-enrichment writes enrichment_pos.tsv, enrichment_neg.tsv, rank_test.tsv, and enrichment_summary.json to results/ (collapsing redundant significant terms that share identical gene sets to the most specific representative term). tabular-summarize writes summary_up.md, summary_up.json, summary_down.md, and summary_down.json, auditing every cited GO ID against the tables (ungrounded_ids and theme_ids_not_significant) and caching Claude replies in results/.claude_cache.db (or --cache-db). Useful options include --condition, --significant-cutoff, --suggestive-cutoff, --system-prompt-file, --max-budget-usd, and --dry-run.

docs.title: Citation
docs.text: The gene summarization approach used in TALISMAN is described further in: Joachimiak MP, Caufield JH, Harris NL, Kim H, Mungall CJ. Gene Set Summarization using Large Language Models. arXiv publication: http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13338
